transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me, I really appreciate your time. I hope I'm not being a bother to you today. 

Um, well, my family actually brought me in. It's just... there was a little misunderstanding at the agricultural fair recently. Nothing malicious, I promise you that. I was giving my talk, and... well, I climbed up onto the tractor. I just wanted to show the crowd this 'new pattern' I’d figured out. I was jerking the controls around to demonstrate, and I guess I just got a bit too caught up in trying to explain it to everyone. 

People started yelling for me to get down, but... I don't know, I just couldn't make myself stop doing it right then. I was just trying to be helpful and show them how it worked, you know? I hope you don't think too badly of me for it. I really do try to be on my best behavior, I didn't mean to cause a fuss. Does that make sense, Doctor?
Has something like this happened to you before?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I... I really don't believe so. I've been farming my whole life, and I've always prided myself on being steady. Reliable, you know? I'm not the sort of man who goes around making a spectacle of himself. 

I mean, sure, sometimes I might get a bit... enthusiastic about the way things connect in my head, maybe talk my family's ear off at the dinner table. But climbing up on equipment in front of all those folks? No, never. 

I really am so embarrassed about the whole thing. I hope you believe me when I say I'm usually a very quiet, rule-abiding fellow. I'm not a troublemaker, I promise. Did... did I answer your question all right, Doctor?
Have you ever done something impulsively, like climbing on the tractor, without thinking it through, in a situation that wasn't related to farming or equipment?

Oh, um... no. No, Doctor, I really don't think so. I've always tried to be a very careful man. You know, look before you leap, that sort of thing. 

I really don't want you to think I'm the type of person who just... acts out or does reckless things. That whole business at the fair, that was just... well, a silly mistake. I just got too wrapped up in trying to help people understand things. But outside of that? No, I stay out of trouble. I go to town for supplies, I go to church, and I come back home to the property. I try my very best to be a good neighbor and keep my head down. 

I don't make a habit of acting without thinking, I swear to you. Is... is that what you were asking? I hope I'm giving you the right answers, I just want to be as helpful to you as I can.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood lately?

Well, um... I suppose my mood's been a little bit... changeable? But nothing too terrible, I promise. I mean, some mornings I wake up and I just feel... wonderful. Like the whole valley is just opening up for me, and I find myself grinning at absolutely nothing at all. It's a nice feeling, really, just being so... so appreciative of the day, you know? 

But, well... I do have to admit, and I'm not proud of this, but if one of the hired hands questions how I'm doing things, or if my wife tells me I need to slow down... I have been snapping at them a bit. Almost like they've insulted the family name or something. I always apologize after, of course! I don't mean to be short with them, I just... I get so focused on all the good work I'm doing. 

It's just a little stress, I'm sure. I really am trying to keep my temper in check. Do you... do you think that's normal for a man my age, Doctor? I hope I'm not sounding like a grumpy old man.
How long have you been noticing these changes in your mood?

Well, um... if I'm being completely honest with you... and I really do want to give you the right answers... it's been going on for a little while now. I suppose, if I look back over this past year or so, these... these stretches where I'm just all charged up, not really sleeping much, just going nonstop... they've probably taken up about ten months of it. 

I know that sounds like a terribly long time to be so keyed up, but I promise I've been getting a lot of good work done around the property! It's not like I'm just running amok, I've been very productive. I hope you don't think I'm foolish for not saying something sooner. I just thought I was having a really good, energetic year for the farm, you know? 

I really hope you don't think worse of me for letting it go on this long. Is... is it okay that I'm just now mentioning it to someone?
Have you ever believed something to be true that others did not believe, something that seemed absolutely real to you but might not be based in reality?

Well, um... I really want to be completely honest with you, Doctor, because I know you're just trying to help me. I wouldn't say I believe things that aren't real. I've always been a very practical man, I promise. But... well, there is one thing, and I really hope you don't think I'm just being paranoid or foolish for saying it. 

My wife, bless her heart, she'll sit me down and show me the lender's plain paperwork, just the standard forms, and she tells me everything is perfectly fine with the property. But... well, I've been looking very closely at our yield maps. And the new drone reports the ag company sends over. There are these... odd numbers in them. They just don't match up right. 

I know how it sounds, I really do, but... I just know they're coded warnings. It's... it's clear to me that folks are trying to take the farm out from under me. I haven't wanted to make a big fuss about it, and I know it upsets my wife when I bring it up, so I try to keep it to myself mostly. I'm not trying to be difficult with her, I'm just trying to protect our land, you know? 

Is... is it okay that I'm paying attention to those things? I just want to make sure I'm doing right by my family and being a good steward of the farm. I hope you can understand where I'm coming from, Doctor. I really am just trying to do my best.
Do you still believe that there are coded warnings in the yield maps and drone reports?

Well, um... I really don't want to sound like a stubborn old mule about this. I know my wife means well when she pulls out the lender's paperwork, and she points to the lines and says, 'Look, everything is fine, the loans are in good standing.' And I want to believe her, I truly do. I don't like upsetting her.

But... yes, sir. I still see them. The numbers on those yield maps and the drone data... they just don't add up the way a normal crop report should. It's... it's like a message, right there in the open if you know how to read it. I still believe it's a warning that they're maneuvering to take the farm from us. 

I'm not trying to be difficult, I promise. I just... I can't unsee what's right there on the page, even if other folks don't see it the same way. Do you think I'm being too hard-headed about it, Doctor? I just want to protect what my family has built, you know? I hope that doesn't make me sound crazy to you.

I really want to please her, and I want to give you the right answer here, too. 

But... well, if I'm being completely honest—and I know you need me to be honest so you can help me—no matter how much I try to just see regular farm data, I just... I know what I'm looking at. The odd numbers in those yield maps and the drone reports, they just jump right out at me. I've tried to tell myself it's nothing, but I know they are coded warnings. It's clear as day that folks are trying to take the farm out from under me. 

I know it probably sounds like I'm not listening to reason, and I hate to disappoint you or my wife. I really do. But I just can't shake it. It feels so real to me. Is... is it terribly wrong of me to still feel that way, even after trying to see it differently? I just want to make sure I'm not being a burden by holding onto this.

And, you know, my wife... she's a saint, she really is. She'll bring out the lender's plain paperwork, just the standard forms, and she'll point right to the bottom line and say, 'See? We're fine.' And I look at it, I really try to just see it her way, because I want her to be happy. I want you to be happy with my progress, too.

I just want to do the right thing.

Well, um... "special powers" is a mighty strong way to put it, Doctor. I really wouldn't want you to think I'm getting a big head or acting like I'm better than anyone else in town. I try to be a humble man, I really do. My wife always says pride comes before a fall, and I agree with her completely. I don't want to come across as boastful to you.

But... well, since you're asking, and I know I need to be completely open if I want to be a good patient for you... I do feel this... this deep certainty. I feel sure that I'm the one farmer in this whole county who can prove a completely new way of growing. It just makes so much sense in my mind, like I can see the connections with the soil and the crops that everyone else is just walking right past. 

I really believe that the university people and those lenders ought to be listening to me instead of doubting me so much. If they'd just sit down and hear me out, they'd see it too. 

I'm sorry if that makes me sound arrogant or full of myself. I really don't mean it that way, I promise. I just see the potential for the land so clearly. Does... does it make me sound foolish to say something like that out loud to you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Do you think you are more intelligent or capable than others in a way that sets you apart from them?

Well, um... I really don't want to sound like I'm putting on airs, Doctor. I know I'm just a simple farmer with a high school education, and I respect the folks who went to college and all. I really do. I don't want you to think I'm sitting out there on my tractor thinking I'm smarter than everybody else in the world. 

But... well, when it comes to the land... my land... I just... I do feel like I'm capable of something that the others aren't seeing. I feel sure I'm the one farmer in the county who can prove a whole new way of growing. It's like I understand the soil in a way that goes beyond what they teach in the books. 

And, well, honestly... I really think the university people and those lenders ought to be listening to me instead of doubting me so much. I know that probably sounds like I'm getting too big for my britches, and I'm sorry if it comes across that way. I just want to be helpful and show them what's possible. Is it okay that I feel that way? I hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression of the kind of man I am.

I don't want to be a big shot, I just want them to see the truth of it. Is it alright that I feel that way? I really don't want you to think I'm getting carried away with myself. I'm just trying to be honest with you.
Do you think you are destined for greatness in farming or any other area of your life?

Oh, um... I feel terrible, Doctor, because I feel like I'm just giving you the exact same answer again, and I really hope you're not getting frustrated with me. I must not be explaining myself very well if you have to keep asking. I'm so sorry about that.
